Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited. Procurement and legal at Lumera are working through the MSA + Order Form and a few redlines popped up that we need your position on before we can route to our CFO. The main items are: 1) explicit ownership for Lumera of output (for patient-facing features), 2) a narrow exception for model retraining that Lumera can opt into for internal analytics (we'd like a defined opt-in flow and a 30-day notice), and 3) feedback/data license for telemetry that allows Redwood to use anonymized signals for quality improvement.

I've attached our annotated redlines (Lumera_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx). Can you confirm Redwood's standard stance on output ownership and the retraining opt-in workflow? If you prefer, we can jump on a quick 30-minute call this week.

Open to compromise here — our procurement team is sensitive to any language that could limit downstream productization.

Thanks Sasha — looping in Ben (legal) and Laura (sales ops / procurement lead) to confirm positions and next steps. Quick notes from product/gtm perspective:

- Output ownership: We typically grant customers a broad right to use generated output in their products, but we do not assign title to derived models. For patient-facing features there are additional safeguards (PHI considerations) — we'll need to ensure those are in the Order Form.
- Retraining opt-in: Redwood is open to an explicit opt-in mechanism that prevents any customer data used for model re-training unless customer marks the environment as "allow_retrain=true" and signs the retrain exhibit. We prefer a one-click portal + signed exhibit rather than an open permissive clause.
- Feedback/telemetry: We can accept an anonymized, aggregated license for product improvement, with clear exclusions for PII/PHI.

Ben/Laura — can you shortlist firm redline language and indicate which of Lumera's asks would require an escalation (e.g., title assignment, permanent exclusivity, on-prem data access)? Sasha — if it helps, Laura can share a procurement checklist that speeds routing.

Best,

Subject: Re: Lumera / Redwood MSA — IP & retraining redlines

Aisha / Laura — reviewed Lumera_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx and flagged the items that are legal-sensitive. High-level:

1) Output ownership / title: Lumera's current redline requests assign ownership/title to all generated output used in product features. We can grant an exclusive-use license for Lumera's internal and customer-facing products, but assignment of title or transfer of models back to Lumera is unacceptable (creates IP and export-control risk). Proposed compromise language attached.

2) Retraining / model improvement: We can support an opt-in retraining exhibit. The exhibit should: require a signed addendum, list data categories allowed, mandate de-identification steps, and include a 30-day notice before any retrain that uses Lumera data. We will also include the ability for Lumera to opt-out later (but opt-in must be affirmative).

3) Feedback & telemetry: Accept anonymized aggregated telemetry with exclusions for PHI/PII and a clear retention cap (e.g., 12 months). We must avoid rights that permit Lumera to block Redwood from using model-level improvements derived from aggregate signals (we need to preserve model improvements for service quality).

Action items: Ben attached a short redline excerpt for approval (redlines_suggestions.docx). If Lumera insists on title assignment, route to L9 counsel for escalation and prepare a commercial concession (price uplift or carveouts).

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Lumera / Redwood MSA — IP & retraining redlines

Sasha — following internal sync, we believe there is a pragmatic path to close this week. Summary of concessions and asks (keeps things short so procurement can circulate):

- Output: Redwood will provide Lumera a perpetual, worldwide, nonexclusive license to use generated output in Lumera products and services. Redwood cannot assign title to models or derivative weights; models produced by Lumera prompts remain Lumera's product output under the license.

- Retraining opt-in: We will add a retrain exhibit to the Order Form. Lumera may opt in by signing the exhibit and toggling the "allow_retrain" flag in the enterprise console. Any retrain that uses Lumera data requires a 30-calendar-day notice and a short data-handling checklist (de-identification + scoped dataset). Lumera can revoke opt-in with a 60-day notice.

- Feedback / telemetry: Redwood may use anonymized, aggregated telemetry for product improvement with a 12 month retention limit and an explicit PHI/PII exclusion. Redwood will not claim ownership of data submitted by Lumera customers.

Attached: Lumera_OrderForm_v3.pdf (this includes the retrain exhibit draft and the license language). If that looks acceptable we can push to DocuSign — link below. If Lumera needs title assignment language, we'll need to discuss a commercial trade (either a per-seat uplift, dedicated model isolation, or escrow).
